differences: Kinematic durations of /f/ (target offset minus target onset, as in the authors' code): the mean is 57.40 ms for #f and 64.27 ms for f#n here, where the paper prints 57.6 and 64.1; the other ten means and all twelve SDs agree to the digits the paper prints.

The paper's 304 /fn/ tokens pool the 154 nonnative-cluster tokens with 150 f#n boundary tokens: all 29 vocoid tokens are cluster tokens, and the 6 phonemic errors are 3 cluster and 3 boundary tokens. The 88% accuracy is therefore pooled; for the 154 cluster tokens alone it is 79% (122 correct).
The paper says 288 tokens were collected per participant (22 nonwords x 8 = 176); the tables hold 279 to 392 tokens per participant because they include other items (/zm/ clusters, real words).

The two tables disagree about the item of 2 tokens (one is FAGBEET in the acoustic table and FNAGBEET in the kinematic table; the other is a nativeCC token in one and a singleton in the other); the acoustic table's labels are kept, as in the authors' code. The two files are sorted differently (neither is in the order of the authors' trial numbers); rows follow the acoustic table, and the trial column gives the order of the authors' trial numbers.
